name: Key Solar Contract and Financing Red Flags in LA County

mainEntity.name: What should I check in a Los Angeles County solar contract to avoid predatory escalators or confusing financing terms?
mainEntity.text: What should I check in a Los Angeles County solar contract to avoid predatory escalators or confusing financing terms?

acceptedAnswer.text: Solar financing contracts in Los Angeles County—whether loans, leases, or power purchase agreements (PPAs)—can be complex. Start by identifying the product type and who owns the system. For leases and PPAs, check the annual escalator: a common 2.9–3.9% yearly increase can outpace utility rate changes and erode long-term savings. For loans, examine the APR, term length, dealer fees, and whether there is a balloon payment or required refinance. Focus on total cost over the full term, not just the advertised monthly payment. Look for prepayment and early payoff clauses—some agreements add hefty fees if you clear the balance early or do not apply tax credits as assumed. Verify whether the contract assumes you will qualify for and use incentives; if not, you may owe more than expected. Also confirm what happens when you sell your home: does the buyer have to assume the agreement, or can you prepay or transfer it easily? Ensure performance guarantees, maintenance responsibilities, and monitoring access are clearly spelled out. Do not sign contracts with blank fields, vague escalator language, or verbal promises not reflected in writing. If any term is unclear, insist on written clarification or a revised contract so you fully understand your obligations and risks.
acceptedAnswer.description: In Los Angeles County solar contracts, scrutinize payment schedules, annual price escalators, prepayment options, total finance charges, and what happens if you sell your home. Avoid agreements with unclear buyout terms, aggressive escalators, or penalties for early payoff that erase the expected energy savings.
